nodes.name: Achieve a Single Trusted Supporter View
nodes.owner: Head of Data, Insight and Fundraising CRM

nodes.name: Adopt Microsoft Dynamics 365 as core CRM platform
nodes.rationale: Legacy CRM was over a decade old, built for direct marketing, and not integrated with digital channels
nodes.options_considered: Retain and extend the legacy CRM; build a bespoke platform; adopt Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud; adopt Microsoft Dynamics 365
nodes.chosen_option: Microsoft Dynamics 365 — best fit for existing Microsoft 365/Azure investment and lower integration overhead
nodes.consequences: Easier: single supporter view across channels, native Power Platform automation, reduced integration cost with other Microsoft services. Harder: licensing cost scales with user count; direct-marketing data required significant cleansing to migrate.

nodes.name: Modernise legacy SQL Server infrastructure via managed service
nodes.rationale: Legacy SQL infrastructure was complex, outdated, and relied on a single point of failure
nodes.options_considered: Do nothing and accept the risk; in-place hardware refresh; managed cloud service; full application re-platform
nodes.chosen_option: Managed service on Azure — addressed the single-point-of-failure risk without the cost/risk of a full re-platform
nodes.consequences: Easier: reduced operational burden on internal IT, built-in DR/failover, predictable running cost. Harder: recurring managed-service cost replaces one-off capital spend; less low-level control over tuning.

nodes.name: Extend to a cloud-native data platform beyond the managed-service intermediary
nodes.rationale: The managed-service approach solved the immediate resilience risk, but reporting and cross-system data needs have grown beyond what a lift-and-shift managed instance comfortably supports
nodes.options_considered: Stay on the current managed service; move to a cloud-native platform (e.g. Azure SQL / Synapse-style); adopt a separate analytics platform alongside the existing service
nodes.chosen_option: Not yet finalised — proposed, pending review
nodes.consequences: Easier (anticipated): elastic scaling for reporting workloads, reduced patching overhead. Harder (anticipated): migration effort from the current managed instance; team upskilling required.

nodes.name: Single Customer View Across Donor & Member Records
nodes.acceptance_criteria: A supporter's full history (donations, membership, grants, communications) is viewable from one screen without switching systems
nodes.rationale: Fragmented records across systems mean staff can't see a supporter's full relationship with RBL, leading to poor donor experience and duplicated outreach

nodes.name: Deduplicate Existing Donor Records Before Go-Live
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Zero duplicate donor records remain in the migrated dataset, verified by matching on name, postcode, and email
nodes.rationale: Historic exports from the legacy CRM and direct-marketing database contain known duplicates that would corrupt the single customer view if migrated as-is

nodes.name: Encrypt All Personal Data At Rest And In Transit
nodes.acceptance_criteria: All systems holding personal data pass an annual encryption audit with no exceptions
nodes.rationale: GDPR Article 32 requires appropriate technical measures; current on-prem systems have inconsistent encryption coverage

nodes.name: Eliminate Single Point of Failure in Core Hosting
nodes.acceptance_criteria: No single server or data centre failure can take down more than one critical system at a time
nodes.rationale: Current on-prem hosting concentrates multiple critical systems on shared infrastructure with no failover

nodes.name: Automated Initial Eligibility Screening for Welfare Grants
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Applications clearly ineligible on stated criteria (e.g. service history mismatch) are flagged before reaching a caseworker, reducing manual triage time
nodes.rationale: Caseworkers currently spend significant time on manual first-pass eligibility checks that could be automated for clear-cut cases

nodes.name: Single Sign-On Across Core Staff Systems
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Staff authenticate once to access CRM, finance, and membership systems without separate logins
nodes.rationale: Staff currently maintain separate credentials for each core system, increasing password fatigue and IT support burden

nodes.name: Real-Time Visibility of Poppy Appeal Fundraising Totals
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Regional fundraising totals are visible to coordinators within 15 minutes of a donation being processed, not next-day
nodes.rationale: Regional coordinators currently rely on next-day batch reports, making it hard to react to slow-starting campaigns during the appeal period
